correctness.rationale: Definitions are explicit. The primary source establishes \(\operatorname{sat}_{<}(n,A)=O(1)\) by an explicit witness. For the pair, a consecutive edge cannot be an edge of \(B\); in \(A\) it must be the unique minedge \((4,5)\), whose deletion leaves \(B\) in the old host. Hence a pair-saturated host has no consecutive isolated vertices. With \(r\) non-isolated and \(z\) isolated vertices, \(z\le r+1\), so \(r\ge(n-1)/2\) and \(2|E(H)|\ge r\), proving \(|E(H)|\ge(n-1)/4\) for all \(n\). No finite computation is used.
